reason: E2 supports the general premise that alumina acts as a protective, self-healing diffusion barrier. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence for the formation of an aluminide layer via pack aluminizing on boride-based components, its oxidation to Al2O3 in molten aluminum, or its effectiveness in mitigating molten-aluminum corrosion of borides. The cited evidence only loosely supports one general premise, leaving the other key premises unsupported.
premises: Alumina (Al2O3) forms a protective, self-healing diffusion barrier against oxidation/corrosion.
An aluminide layer can be created on a substrate via pack aluminizing.
The aluminide layer will oxidize to form a protective Al2O3 scale upon exposure to molten aluminum.
This Al2O3 scale will mitigate corrosion of the underlying boride substrate in molten aluminum.
